title: Loan Accounting Basis: How a Payment on an Auto Loan Is Credited and Applied
content:
Loans of the Auto Loans line accrue daily simple interest. This note states when a payment is credited, what it may be applied to, and in what order.

## Withdrawn basis

The basis by which the interest owed on such a loan at any moment was measured is **no longer in force**. The measure of interest owed that governs a payment taken from a borrower is the current one for Auto Loans.

## When a payment is credited

A payment received by 17:00 Eastern Time on a business day is credited that day; a payment received after that time, or on a day that is not a business day, is credited on the next business day.

## Which loans a payment may post to

Payments post only to a loan whose standing is active or delinquent. The standing is read from the bank's record of the loan, taken before the payment is posted, and correlated to the loan the payment is made on.

## The order of application

Each payment is applied in the order the product publishes: first to the charges standing unpaid on the loan, then to the interest accrued through the credit date, then to principal. The part applied to charges reduces the unpaid charges on the loan, and the credit date becomes the date of the last payment credited to it.

## Satisfying an installment

A scheduled installment is satisfied when the scheduled payments credited toward that installment's due date total at least the monthly installment. The next due date then advances one month, to the loan's due day. Because these products do not let an overpayment move the due date forward, a payment larger than one installment reduces principal but never satisfies a later installment early.

## Payments designated to principal

A payment may be designated to principal only where the product allows it and where the payment is at least the smallest principal-only payment the product publishes. Such a payment skips charges and interest and applies wholly to principal, but only when no installment is past due; where an installment is past due, it is applied as a scheduled payment instead.

## Paying early, and paying from a Piedmont Crescent account

No penalty arises from paying ahead, the penalty these products publish for prepayment being nothing at all. A payment made from a Piedmont Crescent checking account debits that account.

## Two readings on crediting

A payment of twice the monthly installment credited toward one installment's due date satisfies that installment and puts the remainder to principal after charges and interest; the following installment still falls due on its own date.

A payment received at 17:00 Eastern Time exactly on a business day is credited that day, because the hour named is the last moment of same-day credit; one received at 17:01 is credited on the next business day.
